full_judgment:
The petitioner before us Md. Ali Ashgar filed an application under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which was registered Criminal Case No. 21P of 1994 in the Court of the Magistrate, First Class, Court No. 3; Naogaon and whereupon the learned Magistrate by the initio order dated 19.1.94 directed officer-in-charge of the Local Police Station to enquire into the matter and to submit a report. By the same order the learned "Magistrate directed the officer-in-charge of the local police station to maintain status quo obviously in respect of the possession in the case land. It appears that 60 day; thereafter the learned Magistrate passed an order on 9.4.94 initiating a proceeding under Section 145, Cr.P. Code with the remark "মামলাটি ফৌঃ কাঃ বিঃ ১৪৫ ধারায় স্থানান্তর করা হইল" He then attached the case land and appointed officer-in-charge of the local police station as receiver thereof. 

 3. Mr. Sultan Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, at first draws our attention to the reasoning’s of the learned Sessions Judge in the impugned judgment which are that after the expiry of the statutory time-limit of 60 days from the date of initial order passed in a proceeding under section 144 of the Code Criminal Procedure the said proceeding could not be converted into a proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as the proceedings under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure were then dead. The learned Advocate then submits that for all purposes and intents the impugned order dated 9.4.94 passed by the learned Magistrate is a fresh order initiating a proceeding under section 145 of the Code Criminal Procedure on the basis of the police report and a sentence in the order of the learned Magistrate quoted by us above do not vitiate the proceeding itself and that even accepting the said sentence is inseparable from the entire order dated 9.4.94, it can at best be said that the order is an irregular one and then in that case it is curable under section 537 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 4. Mr. Lutfor Rahman Mandal, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party Nos. 1-29, submits that the said sentence in the order of the learned Magistrate has made the entire order illegal more so when the impugned order was passed in the file of the case under section 144 of the Code 'of Criminal Procedure and as such it is not an independent proceeding initiated by the learned Magistrate, but a continuation or conversion of the proceeding previously initiated by the learned Magistrate under section 144. In support of his submission Mr. Mondal cites a decision of a Division Bench of the Dhaka High Court reported in 5DLR. at page 162D wherein it has been held that after the expiry of the statutory time-limit in a proceeding under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure there remained nothing before the learned Magistrate on which he could start a proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 5. We are unable to accept the submission of Mr. Mondal. The learned Magistrate initiated the proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on the basis of the police report which was placed before him on that date i.e. on 9.4.94 and therefore it cannot be said that the learned Magistrate passed the order on 9.4.94 in continuation of the proceeding under section 144 which was then dead. The decision cited by Mr. Mondal does not disclose the fact like the instant case as to whether the learned Magistrate passed the order on the basis of a recent report that a dispute likely to cause a breach of peace existed concerning the case land in question. It is crystal clear from the order dated 9.4.94 passed by the learned Magistrate that on that date there existed a dispute likely to cause breach of peace concerning the case land and as such some of the words in the impugned order of the learned Magistrate does not make the order as illegal one as canvassed by Mr. Mandal. Therefore, it must be held that the insertion of the word “স্থানান্তর” is an irregularity which is curable under section 537 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 6. Further it is well-settled that the exercise of power under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is discretionary while under section 145 it is mandatory as the words "Magistrate may" and "he shall" have been used respectively in section 144 and 145. Thereafter, whether action has previously been taken under section 144 or not, the Magistrate must act under section 145 if condition as to its application exists and must take action either in suppression or in continuation or in the absence of any order passed under section 144. In view of this legal position we further hold that the learned Sessions Judge was wrong to set aside the order dated 9.4.94.
